cards.text: Friend, David is king over Israel now, and he asks about the house of Saul, Israel's king before him. Is there anyone left? A brand new king asking where the old king's family is? I'd be packing my apron.

cards.question: King David wants to find anyone left from the house of Saul. What does he want to do for them?
True or false: David says he wants to do this for the sake of Jonathan, Saul's son.

cards.text: They summon Ziba, a servant from Saul's house, and he tells the king, 'I am your servant,' just like that. Then David asks his question again, and this time he calls it the kindness of God.

cards.question: Ziba tells King David there's still one left from Saul's house: Jonathan's ___.

cards.text: Jonathan's son, Ziba says, and he is lame in both feet. No follow-up questions, no paperwork, just the king saying, 'Where is he?'

cards.question: Where does Ziba say Jonathan's son is staying?

cards.text: He's at the house of Machir son of Ammiel, so King David has him brought from Lo-debar. His name is Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, grandson of Saul.

cards.question: Mephibosheth is brought in front of King David. What does he do?

cards.text: David says, 'Mephibosheth!' and he answers with the line Ziba used, 'I am your servant,' from the floor. Full name, from the KING, in front of everybody? I'd be facedown too, apologizing for things I hadn't even done yet.

cards.question: Mephibosheth is facedown in front of King David, calling himself the king's servant. What does David tell him?

answers.text: Why did you hide from me

cards.text: David says he will surely show him kindness for the sake of his father Jonathan. And friend, he is NOT talking about a nice handshake and a pat on the back.

cards.question: David says he will restore to Mephibosheth all the ___ of his grandfather Saul.
True or false: David tells Mephibosheth he can eat at the king's table on feast days.

cards.text: ALWAYS. At the king's table, ALWAYS. Mephibosheth bows down again and asks why the king would show regard for someone like him.

cards.question: Mephibosheth asks why King David would show regard for him. What does he call himself?

cards.text: A dead dog. I know that talk, friend: back in the drawer, I called myself a worn-out stamper so often the dust started agreeing with me.
Then the king summons Ziba. He tells him he has given Saul's grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.

cards.question: True or false: David tells Ziba that Mephibosheth will work Saul's land himself.

cards.text: Ziba and his sons and servants will work the ground and bring in the harvest, and Ziba has fifteen sons and twenty servants. I fill cookie boxes with a mustache, friend, and Ziba's got a whole TEAM.

cards.question: Ziba says he'll do all the king commanded. How does Mephibosheth eat at David's table?

answers.text: Like one of the king's own sons
Like one of the king's servants
Like one of the king's soldiers

cards.question: Mephibosheth has a young son named Mica, and everyone who lives in Ziba's house is Mephibosheth's ___.
True or false: After all this, Mephibosheth goes back to live in Lo-debar.

cards.text: Mephibosheth lives in Jerusalem, because he always eats at the king's table, and he was lame in both feet. Brought out of Lo-debar to a seat at the king's table for good? Friend, that one gets me right in the dough.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Friend, David is king…', 'Is there anyone left?', 'A brand new king asking…?' and 'I'd be packing my apron.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage without references: that David is king over Israel and that Saul was Israel's king before him (for example 2 Samuel 5:3 and 1 Samuel 10:24). The card cites only 2 Samuel 9:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls David 'a brand new king.' By this point David has reigned for some time. The chapters before this one show him capturing Jerusalem and winning wars against many nations (2 Samuel 5, 8). This is stated as a fact, not kept inside a clear joke.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke 'No follow-up questions… just the king saying, "Where is he?"' contradicts itself, because 'Where is he?' is a follow-up question. A stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This story card doesn't move the passage forward. It repeats 'A dead dog,' which the baker already answered on card 6, and then adds only a joke. No new part of 2 Samuel 9:8 or the verses after it is told.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new habit to his drawer backstory: that he called himself a worn-out stamper 'so often' while in the drawer. The backstory has him say 'worn-out stamper' once, to the angel. Invented habits are allowed only around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
